newsitem.title: FRANCE: Valeo Jan-Aug sales up 17 pct at 19 bln Ffr.
newsitem.headline: Valeo Jan-Aug sales up 17 pct at 19 bln Ffr.

text.p: Valeo chairman Noel Goutard said on Thursday that the car part manufacturer's sales rose 17 percent in the first eight months of the year to 19 billion francs ($3.7 billion).
He said the group maintained its objective for full-year turnover of 28.5 billion francs despite a doubtful fourth quarter.

"We haven't begun the second half badly," Goutard told a news conference. "We're maintaining our objective for 28.5 billion francs annual turnover despite the question mark hanging over the fourth quarter," he said.
The October-December quarter is expected to be difficult for the French car industry given the expiry on September 30 of a state rebate scheme that has underpinned demand.
"I can't tell you we are going to have as strong a profit increase in the second half as in the first half," Goutard said, citing the uncertainty about prospects for the final quarter.
Valeo reported a 31 percent rise in pre-exceptional income to 656 million francs in the first six months of 1996.
Goutard declined to give any full-year profit forecast.
He said, however, the currency turmoil that had a negative 500 million franc impact on its turnover last year had eased.
"This year we are talking about an impact of some tens of millions of francs, hardly worth mentioning on our turnover," he said.
Buyout speculation that has hung over Valeo ever since shareholder Cerus said in February that it would consider offers for its 28 percent stake has not disrupted morale at the company, he said.
"These results were clearly generated by a motivated staff," he said.
He declined to address questions about industry minister Franck Borotra's comments in a newspaper on Thursday in which he said he hoped a French buyer for Cerus's stake would be found this month.
